{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"The rope twitched. Far below the stairs, something answered with a hollow knock.

Mara wound the thread twice around her fist and pulled. The other Mara stumbled forward, but the rope at its wrist drew tight, holding it short of the doorway. Its borrowed face changed. For an instant it was the boy’s, eyes wide and pleading.

“Open the door,” it whispered.

The bolt scraped from the kitchen side.

“Leave it,” Mara called. “Both of you, leave it shut.”

A small voice answered through the wood. “The cup’s in here.”

Mara looked at the rope disappearing down the stairs. She remembered setting the empty cup on the kitchen table when she came in from the well. She had not noticed the water gathering beneath it.

“Is anyone touching it?” she asked.

“No,” said the girl. “It keeps turning over.”

The lantern guttered. The thing caught its handle, and green fire ran along the rope toward the stairs. Mara let go of the handle and seized the rope instead. It was cold and coarse, exactly as it had felt at the well. She pulled with both hands.

From the kitchen came the clatter of a cup hitting the floor. The rope went slack. The other Mara fell against the threshold, its wet fingers closing on nothing.

“Now,” Mara said.

The key turned. The door opened just wide enough for the girl to thrust out a tin cup. Mara dropped the rope into it. The cup grew heavy in her hands, and from its dark interior came the sound of a bucket striking stone."}
